articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the April 1995 issue of "SJAA EPHEMERIS," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It is identified as Volume 6, Number 4 of the publication.

articles.title: The Eyepiece
articles.summary: This 'Eyepiece' column by Bob Madden reflects on observing opportunities and shares the editor's personal experience with a disk drive crash, emphasizing the importance of data backup. It also highlights member Bob Ashford's successful astronomy program for schoolchildren and provides a comprehensive calendar of upcoming events for April and May, including star parties, general meetings, observational astronomy classes, and a swap/auction, alongside an announcement of increased membership dues.

articles.title: Forty Years Ago this month
articles.summary: This article recounts an Astronomy Club meeting held forty years prior, detailing presentations on Ursa Major and optical finders, a demonstration of a homemade "Tin Can Planetarium," and a discussion regarding the club's incorporation. The meeting concluded with observing canceled due to weather, and lists the club's officers at the time.

articles.title: January 26, 1995
articles.summary: A letter from a science teacher at Bernal commends Bob Ashford, an associate of the San Jose Astronomical Association, for his excellent and engaging presentation on astronomy and a guided tour of the solar system to approximately 300 students. The teacher highly praises his crisp, cogent, and enthralling commentary, recommending him for accolades.

articles.title: Fremont Peak Feb 25, 1995
articles.summary: Mark Wagner provides a detailed report of an observing session at Fremont Peak on February 25, 1995, highlighting initial excellent transparency that allowed for clear views of objects like Orion, Mars, M42, and the Eskimo Nebula. Despite deteriorating conditions and eventual dense fog by late evening, a significant number of galaxies were observed and meticulously cataloged. The report also lists the presence of other amateur astronomers, their equipment, and notes the use of a computer for enhanced observing.

articles.title: Grinding and Testing Mirrors
articles.summary: The author recounts their experience grinding a 5.5-inch telescope mirror with assistance from Paul Barton, using a geared-down pottery wheel for the initial shaping. Facing difficulties with a sensitive Foucault tester during the polishing phase, the author decided to build a Ronchi tester, gathering design information from Paul Zurakowski at Chabot Mirror Lab. The article details the construction of the Ronchi tester's light source and explains how to interpret the patterns for spherical and parabolic mirror surfaces to assess the mirror's figure.

articles.title: On Being A Kid Observer — Novices —
articles.summary: The author recounts his early experiences as a young amateur astronomer, detailing his progression through various low-cost telescopes and the initial challenges he faced. He then offers practical advice for new observers, advocating for essential resources like star charts and astronomy books, and recommending a systematic approach to observation, including journaling and using a substantial finder scope for deep-sky objects, to accelerate learning.

articles.title: Project Astro Needs You
articles.summary: Project Astro, a program by the Astronomical Society of the Pacific and funded by the National Science Foundation, seeks to pair amateur and professional astronomers with 4th-9th grade teachers. Participants will receive training and commit to multiple classroom and observational visits over a six-month period to foster astronomy education. Interested individuals are encouraged to call Jessica Richter for an application.

articles.title: April 8th, 1995
articles.summary: The document announces an event held on April 8th, 1995, featuring a swap meet from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM, followed by an auction starting at 6:00 PM. Hosted at Hogue Park near Hwy. 17 and Camden Ave., the event was sponsored by the San Jose Astronomical Association and encouraged attendees to bring items for swapping or selling. The document also includes directions and a note about an "Ephemeris" on page 4 for April 1995, implying it's part of a larger publication or flyer.

articles.title: Directions to HOUGE PARK
articles.summary: This document provides directions to Houge Park and details for the 1995 Bay Area Astronomical Auction, including a registration form. It also features the 1995 calendar for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), listing dates for general meetings, Houge Park Star Parties, and Observational Astronomy Classes from April to September.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Status
articles.summary: This document, titled "Telescope Loaner Status" by Paul Barton, provides an update on the availability and current loan status of various telescopes. It details which instruments are currently loaned out, their respective due dates, and which are available for borrowing by members. Instructions are provided for interested members to contact Paul Barton to get on a general or specific telescope waiting list.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: This document is a classifieds section titled "ASTRO ADS," offering free advertisements for noncommercial sellers of astronomically related products and services. It provides submission guidelines, including a monthly deadline and contact information for the editor. The bulk of the content consists of listings for used astronomical equipment, such as telescopes, eyepieces, and ATM stock, with details on specifications, condition, price, and seller contact information.

articles.title: Lunar Phase Date Rise Trans Set
articles.summary: This document provides a tabular listing of the four primary lunar phases: First Quarter, Full Moon, Last Quarter, and New Moon. For each phase, it specifies the exact time and date of occurrence, along with the moon's corresponding rise, transit, and set times. This data is essential for tracking the lunar cycle and planning astronomical observations.

articles.title: Nearer Planets:
articles.summary: This document presents an astronomical ephemeris for the "Nearer Planets"—Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn—for three distinct dates (7th, 17th, 27th) of an unspecified month. For each celestial body, it provides apparent magnitude, distance in Astronomical Units (where applicable), and three time values, likely representing rise, transit, and set. Additionally, it includes positional data and similar time information for the Sun (SOL).

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight:
articles.summary: The document presents a tabular listing of the start and end times for astronomical twilight. These times are provided for three specific Julian Dates, detailing the duration of this astronomical phenomenon.

articles.title: Sidereal Time:
articles.summary: This document provides sidereal time calculations for specific dates in April 1995, showing transit right ascension at local midnight. It also details the observing conditions for the 'Darkest Saturday Night' on April 29, 1995, listing times for sunset, twilight end, moonset, and dawn begin.

articles.title: TIMES AND DATES ARE PACIFIC DAYLIGHT
articles.summary: This brief note specifies that all presented times and dates are in Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), with individual times representing local civil time. It credits the derivation of these values to two resources: "Astronomy with Your Personal Computer" by Peter Duffet-Smith and "MacEphem" by Elwood Charles Downey.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and board of directors for an organization. It includes their titles, names, and contact phone numbers for various leadership roles such as President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, and multiple Directors.

articles.title: Ephemeris Contributors
articles.summary: This document provides a contact list, detailing the names and phone numbers of individuals who contribute to ephemeris data, including Don Machholtz, Jim Van Nuland, Richard Stanton, and Paul Barton. It also lists Bob Madden as the editor with his contact information.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: Don Machholz's 'COMET COMMENTS' column celebrates its 200th issue, reflecting on its evolution from a handwritten local newsletter addition in 1978 to an internationally distributed resource for comet observers. The article details its growth from being mailed to various astronomy clubs to being available on electronic bulletin boards and America OnLine, while also providing an update on Periodic Comet d'Arrest. Machholz expresses his continued enjoyment in writing the column and its utility for readers and observers worldwide.

articles.title: EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document provides a detailed ephemeris for the periodic comet 6P/d'Arrest, listing its celestial coordinates (Right Ascension, Declination), elongation, sky visibility, and apparent magnitude for dates between March 24 and May 13. It also includes key orbital elements for the comet, such as its perihelion date, distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document outlines the membership options and application process for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing different fee structures for standard, junior, and magazine-inclusive memberships. It provides contact information for submitting applications and inquiries, including a mailing address for the treasurer and an information hotline. The document also mentions 'EPHEMERIS' as the SJAA's monthly publication, inviting member submissions.
